newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt welcomes passage of video-on-demand bill.
newsitem.headline: HK govt welcomes passage of video-on-demand bill.

text.p: The Hong Kong government on Wednesday welcomed the passage of a bill by legislators which will allow for video-on-demand television services.

"Video-on-demand offers the potential for a wide range of innovative multimedia services, including new ways of delivering television programmes to the home," said Chau Tak Hay, Secretary for Broadcasting, Culture and Sport.
"The licensing framework we have now put in place provides certainty to investors, as well as the assurance to viewers that the content of programme services will be properly regulated."
The Television (Amendment) Bill 1996 was passed by legislators on Wednesday.
Chau said his branch was now working towards putting the detailed regulations in place and will invite applications for licences within the next few months.
The government also planned to issue two licences although all applications will be considered on their own merit.

Shares of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd edged up on Monday after it secured a local film supply for its interactive television services and planned to launch its video-on-demand services in July, brokers said.
